spans.s:
baindava-śarīra
(‘body comprising the बिन्दु’)
------------------------------------------
Among the several schools of शैविस्म्, the Siddha school has a concept of मुक्ति or लिबेरतिओन्, peculiar to itself. मुक्ति is incomplete if it is confined only to the elimination of future births after death. It becomes complete only when death here is also transcended. A sādhaka or aspirant of the Siddha School, through appropriate exercise and spiritual practice, is able to transmute every cell in his body so that it is transformed from अशुद्ध-माया (impure māya or nature)-state to śuddha-māyā (pure māyā or nature)-state. This transformed body which is incorruptible, is called ‘praṇavatanu’ (body of प्रणव or Om) or ‘baindava-śarīra’ (body comprising the बिन्दु or divine power—śakti). Then he becomes a ‘jīvanmukta’ (one liberated even while living).
See also SIDDHA-DARŚANA.
